headline: Record quarter beats guidance on organic and acquired growth
summary_short: Amphenol's Q2 2026 net sales rose 55% y/y to $8.76B (30% organic), with GAAP diluted EPS up 59% to $1.37 and Adjusted Diluted EPS up 67% to $1.35, both above the high end of prior guidance. Q3 2026 guidance calls for $9.3B-$9.4B sales and $1.40-$1.42 Adjusted Diluted EPS.
summary_long: Net sales rose 55% y/y (30% organic) to $8.76B, driven by exceptional IT datacom growth and CommScope, El.Com, and Wilder Technologies acquisitions. GAAP operating margin expanded to 29.5% from 25.1%, including an $80M tariff-recovery benefit; Adjusted Operating Margin reached 29.8%. GAAP diluted EPS rose 59% to $1.37 and Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 67% to $1.35, both above the high end of prior guidance. Orders were $10.7B, a 1.23:1 book-to-bill. Cash fell to $4.73B from $11.13B at year-end after $10.68B of acquisition spending YTD, offset partly by $4.93B of new debt. Q3 2026 guidance: $9.3B-$9.4B sales, $1.40-$1.42 Adjusted EPS. CommScope's FY2026 outlook raised to $4.6B sales / $0.30 EPS accretion from $4.1B / $0.15.

drivers.explanation: Driven by strong organic growth across most end markets -- especially exceptional IT datacom growth -- plus contributions from the acquisition program (CommScope, El.Com, Wilder Technologies).
Tracks the operating-income and net-income growth described elsewhere; includes an $0.04/share net tariff-recovery benefit and $0.03/share of discrete tax charges.

Adjusted operating income rose faster than EPS because the Adjusted Effective Tax Rate rose to 27.0% on a shift of income to higher-tax jurisdictions and a China tax matter, plus more diluted shares outstanding.
Not explained beyond the overall sales growth described for the quarter.
Higher sales volumes and an $80M net IEEPA tariff-recovery benefit; not further decomposed in the release.
Adjusted Operating Margin reached 29.8%, inclusive of the same $80M net tariff recoveries cited for GAAP operating income.
Operating-income growth partly offset by higher interest expense on acquisition debt and a higher tax provision, including a $39.0M discrete foreign-tax-reserve charge.
Six-month acquisition spending of $10.68B (mainly the CommScope close) exceeded $2.68B of operating cash flow and $4.93B of new debt issuance.
Growth reflects retained-earnings accumulation from net income, partially offset by treasury-stock buybacks and dividends paid.

CEO Adam Norwitt framed the quarter as record sales and EPS exceeding the high end of guidance, crediting organic IT-datacom strength, the acquisition program, and record orders (1.23:1 book-to-bill).
